Adversarial tweets (retweets) crafted to fool stock prediction models

datasets: stock prediction dataset consisting of 10,824 instances including relevant tweets and numerical features of 88 stocks from 2014 to 2016

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated dataset references to single canonical name, deduplicated model names, and normalized output description
Normalized 'F1 drop' to 'F1 score' as the paper uses F1 score as the base metric and measures the drop
No LLM-based evaluation is used in this paper - the paper focuses on adversarial attacks against financial prediction models
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper - evaluation is entirely automated using metrics

overall_notes: This paper focuses on adversarial attacks against stock prediction models using modified tweets. While it generates text (adversarial tweets), the primary contribution is in the attack methodology rather than NLG evaluation. The automatic metrics used (ASR, F1, PnL) are specifically designed for evaluating the attack effectiveness rather than general NLG quality.
